sentences.text:
This is the third bail application filed by applicant under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code,
1973 as he is implicated in connection with Crime No.81/2022 registered at Police Station - Neemuch Kant (Cantt.), District - Neemuch (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC.

entities.text: Police Station - Neemuch Kant (Cantt.), District - Neemuch
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 10/02/2022.
The allegation against the applicant is of defalcation of a sum of Rs.5 lakhs, which was obtained from the complainant on the pretext of providing her a Government job.

Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the charge-sheet has already been filed and the applicant is lodged in jail since 10.02.2022 and his wife is also suffering from Uterine Fibroid, for which she is required to undergo operation.

It is further submitted that the status report has also Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35874017/
1 been called in which it is stated that till date none of the witnesses have appeared in the Trial Court.

entities.text: Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the applicant would abide by all the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.

Counsel for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for grant of bail is made out especially when the applicant's earlier applications have already been dismissed.

On due consideration of submissions and on perusal of the case-diary as also the medical documents filed by the applicant in the Court regarding his wife's ailment and also taking note of the fact that not a single witness has been examined, this Court is inclined to allow the application, subject to deposit of Rs.3 lakhs in the Trial Court.

Accordingly, without commenting anything on merits of the matter, the present application for grant of bail is allowed, subject to deposit of an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees three lakhs) by the applicant in the trial Court, out of which, Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand) shall be deposited upfront before his release i.e. at the time of furnishing the bail bond in a fixed deposit in a nationalized bank and producing the receipt/certificate of the same before the concerned trial Court and rest of Rs.2,50,000/-(Rupees two lakh fifty thousand) to be deposited by the applicant in five equal installments of Rs.50,000/- each within a period of five months from the date of his release,
in a fix deposit in a nationalized bank and producing the receipt/certificate of the same before the concerned trial Court and the said amount shall be subject to the final outcome of the case by the trial Court.

The deposit receipt/certificate so produced by the applicant shall be endorsed by the learned Judge of the lower Court to be 'furnished towards the bail of the applicant and shall be subject to the final decision of the case by the trial Court'.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance, as and when directed and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Bahar Gopal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35874017/
